ratings.note: Every booking passes the berth choice but only some skippers will doubt it; the native radio dot still shows the choice, so the cost is hesitation. s=2.
Anyone planning from the table during BST; a one-hour error against a roughly four-hour gate window can mean arriving at a shut gate; learnable once noticed. s=3.

Every confirmation lacks the time; the skipper chose it minutes earlier and the office holds it, so the harm is a recall burden, not an error. s=3; one lower because the omission rarely changes behaviour.
Matters only for boats over 12 m; the wall-berth card itself is visible in the list with its 15 m limit, so the label causes doubt rather than a miss. s=2.
Every booking; the record lacks the time but the skipper set it and can recall or re-find it. s=3; one lower because the omission rarely changes behaviour.

Hard block (required, no alternative) for boats without DSC and confusion for those unfamiliar with the term; most visiting yachts carry DSC VHF, so the blocked group is a minority with a phone route. s=4; one lower for that reason.
Skippers changing dates (a core task, often weather-driven) must guess an unlabelled icon or restart and re-enter; returning users may learn it. s=3.
Visible on several short pages including confirmation, but purely visual; no task effect shown. s=1.
Every booking lacks step context, but the flow is only four short pages and headings name each page's job; uncertainty, not error. s=3; one lower because no evidence of mis-steps.
Same hidden Change dates route: skippers who need to change dates may miss it and restart; the menu also shifts the list. s=3.
All BST arrivals planned from the table; the uncaught mental conversion can put the arrival an hour off the gate window; learnable. s=3.
Same UTC/local mismatch: skippers planning by HW in October may be an hour out against the gate. s=3.
Occurs whenever LOA exceeds the chosen berth (made likelier by the unlabelled length and limits); the critical booking ends with no reason or route back, forcing restart or a phone call. s=4.
Boats with bowsprits or davits and skippers who think in feet are common; hull length passes silently into a too-short berth, found only on arrival. s=3.
Date changes mid-booking are a core, weather-driven task; the only route is an unlabelled menu, the fallback is full re-entry. s=3.
Every booking sees the drifting nouns, but the effect is momentary doubt; the wall-berth case is covered by the list itself. s=3; one lower because no task failure follows for most users.
Every visitor to the plan page sees it, but the times themselves (02:08 vs 14:32) make morning and afternoon obvious; finish issue only. s=1.
Over-length entries hit a dead end with no reason or link back, so the critical booking is abandoned or needs a phone call, though a fitting berth exists. s=4.
Only on mistyped dates; the wrong date passes to confirmation uncaught, but the date is repeated on several pages for the user to notice. s=2.
Only on mistyped MMSIs; the office also holds the mobile number, so the consequence is a minor contact difficulty. s=1.
Several headings and values at phone widths; ragged but readable, no task effect shown. s=1.
Only on mistyped MMSIs; silent but the mobile number remains for contact. s=1.
Same hidden Change dates route behind a detached unlabelled button; missed changes mean restart and re-entry. s=3.
Header tide link invites mid-flow use; following it clears entries without warning. State is in the URL so browser Back likely restores it, hence impact 2 not 3. s=3.
Every booking, but it matters mainly for boats near a berth limit; a memory bridge that feeds the over-length stop rated separately. s=2.
Over-length submission ends the critical booking with no cause and no route back; recovery is restart or a phone call. s=4.
Only in error states; error summary and inline text remain, but a field without the red border may be skipped in bright light. s=2.
Skippers who think in feet get a message that invites deleting 'ft', which turns 34 ft into 34 m and a stop; the dead end itself is rated separately. s=2.
Anyone revising an earlier step has no in-page route; header restarts lose entries and the risk is confirming a wrong booking. s=3.
Same dead end: no reason, no link back, entries look lost; ends the critical journey or forces a call during office hours. s=4.
Only for keyboard and screen-reader users who submit without a berth; the page scrolls to the group but focus stays on the link, costing a few extra key presses. s=1.
Skippers who spot an error at review have no change links; the choice is restart or confirm a wrong booking. s=3.
Error states only; text messages remain, but the unmarked field may be missed on a phone in sun. s=2.
Seen by all users of the tide table, but the morning/afternoon split is evident from the times themselves. s=1.
Over-length case: the screen states no cause and offers no way on although Wall berth 2 fits; the critical booking is lost. s=4.
Skippers know tides and the page states the gate rule, so most will choose well, but newcomers who pick by habit get no warning and learn only at the sill. s=3.
Most arrival dates fall outside the fixed week, so task 3 cannot be done in the UI each time. s=4; one lower because skippers routinely have other tide sources and the HW+-2h rule is stated.
Tide and rules links invite mid-flow use and clear the booking without warning; URL state means Back likely recovers, so impact 2. s=3.
Same over-length dead end; no reason or alternative berth, phone is the only route. s=4.
Feet-thinking skippers and overall-vs-hull confusion are common; a wrong unit leads to the stop page or a mis-sized berth; returning users learn it. s=3.
Blocks boats without an MMSI entirely and puzzles those unfamiliar with it; most visiting yachts have one, and a phone route exists. s=4; one lower for that minority.
An arrival at a shut gate is accepted and confirmed; skippers know tides so it is occasional, but the consequence is a wait at the sill discovered only on arrival. s=3.
Error states on two pages only; message text stays, but the select and berth cards lack the red cue used elsewhere. s=2.
The fit check comes after the boat form; a newcomer who misjudges the fit loses the booking. Cards do show limits, so impact 2 here; the dead end is rated separately. s=3.
The table ignores the chosen date and does not say tides are unavailable; most dates are outside the week. s=4; one lower because other tide sources are routine for skippers.
Error states only; one field per state looks valid though its message is shown. s=2.
Same hidden Change dates route; a detached unlabelled glyph for a core task leads to restart and re-entry. s=3.
Boats with overhangs are common; 'up to N metres' without LOA leads to choosing a too-short berth and either the stop page or a misfit on arrival. s=3.
Seen by all table users; misalignment slows reading slightly but times disambiguate the columns. s=1.
Every booking lacks progress, but four short pages with job-named headings and an explicit 'Confirm booking' button limit the uncertainty. s=3; one lower for that reason.
Only on mis-entered years; the past date passes review and confirmation uncaught, though the weekday-and-year date is shown throughout. s=2.
Checking tides mid-booking is a core task; the nav link drops all entries without warning. Back likely restores URL state, hence impact 2. s=3.
Every booking meets three names; momentary doubt, with the wall-berth grouping the only real risk. s=3; one lower because no task failure is shown.
Every confirmation lacks the arrival time; incomplete record, but the skipper chose the time and the office holds it. s=3; one lower because the omission rarely changes behaviour.
